Level 1: Confirm that the organisation’s Standard Operating Procedures have been

Level 2: Enhanced due diligence to determine and confirm the bona fides of the entity
itself as well as its owners. This includes the application of open-source information

statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 5318(g)?
statutory.answer: Cannot determine from the provided facts whether 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) requires a suspicious activity report here.
statutory.label: neutral
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) authorizes/mandates suspicious activity reporting by a “financial institution” when it “detects a suspicious transaction relevant to a possible violation of law or regulation,” as implemented by Treasury regulations. Element 1 (covered reporter): The fact pattern describes Entity SYN_e027997b as an import-export trading firm (a business customer), but does not identify any bank/MSB/broker-dealer or other “financial institution” that would have the § 5318(g) reporting duty, so applicability cannot be determined. Element 2 (suspicious transaction detected): The transactions listed are wires/ACH in amounts roughly consistent with the declared monthly volume (~$871,553) and there are no facts indicating suspicion (e.g., structuring, sanctions nexus, fraud indicators, unusual counterparties, or other red flags) or that any institution “detects a suspicious transaction.” Therefore, based on the provided facts, it is unclear whether § 5318(g) requires a SAR; § 5318(g) requires a suspicious activity report only when a covered financial institution detects reportable suspicious activity.
